prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: single transparent tree sprite for a 2.5D medieval world map
Primary request: One mature temperate broadleaf tree, oak/birch-like, realistic restrained painted ink-and-wash aesthetic reminiscent of a medieval Battle Brothers world map.
Scene/backdrop: True transparent background, isolated asset.
Subject: A compact single mature tree with a broad organic asymmetrical crown, distinct branching foliage cluster volumes, finely varied muted olive and sage green foliage, and a warm brown slender visible trunk. Balanced natural proportions; avoid spherical lollipop shape. No root dirt mound.
Composition/framing: Fixed orthographic three-quarter isometric view from 50 degrees elevation above horizontal. Show the crown top and the front trunk. One tree only, completely framed with generous transparent margin; trunk base positioned bottom center. Not a forest, not multiple trees.
Style/medium: Restrained realistic naturalistic painted ink and wash, subtle crisp ink contour and fine leaf-cluster texture, suited to a small strategy-game sprite. Muted natural colors compatible with realistic ground textures, no cartoon exaggeration.
Lighting/mood: Soft daylight from top left, gentle self shading. No external cast ground shadow.
Constraints: Preserve clean actual alpha transparency, no white matte, no checkerboard, no horizon, no ground, no background, no text, no watermark, no border. Do not include any other object.

alpha_validation.method: sips metadata; read-only PNG pixel decoding with Python standard library; Pillow unavailable

visual_inspection.findings: One mature broadleaf tree with varied asymmetrical muted olive crown, branch volumes, visible warm-brown trunk, full framing, no ground mound or external shadow. No matte/background/text/border.
concerns: Perspective appears lower than requested 50-degree elevation; exact camera angle is not independently measurable.
Nearly all subject pixels have partial alpha; map composite appearance needs parent integration inspection.
